extracted.intended_audience: federal agency staff, policymakers, stakeholders, and the public interested in administrative rulemaking and notice-and-comment processes
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and improving federal agencies' online regulatory comment systems to prevent abuse (fake comments, profanity, flooding, identity theft) and to preserve meaningful public participation in rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguard online comment systems from abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: When the online comment system is not safeguarded from abuse, it limits Americans’ ability to engage in the rulemaking process and provide meaningful input on proposed rules being developed by federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Subcommittee's review demonstrated that agencies, across administrations, have not taken sufficient action to identify or prevent abuse. Improving safeguards is necessary so the comment process "works in the public’s interest."

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and prevent posting of fake comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies must take action to identify or prevent the posting of fake comments on their regulatory comment system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Subcommittee found agencies "have not taken sufficient action to identify or prevent the posting of fake comments on their regulatory comment system," including rampant use of stolen identities to post comments with no recourse for victims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer abuses to law enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should refer fake or abusive comments to law enforcement when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Subcommittee found agencies do not refer such comments to law enforcement; referral is presented as an expected corrective step when abuse is detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screen for and remove profane, abusive, and threatening content
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should detect and remove comments containing profanity, threats of violence, and otherwise abusive content from public comment systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report found "more than 100,000 comments containing profanity and threats of violence" and that major systems "play host to a significant amount of profane and abusive content." Agencies vary in whether and how they screen and remove such content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screen for and remove sensitive information
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should screen comments for sensitive information and remove it when posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Subcommittee noted some agencies "regularly screen for profanity and sensitive information," but practices are inconsistent and some agencies that screen do not always remove sensitive content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement uniform policies and consistent posting practices
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a uniform policy across agencies governing whether comments are posted as received, screened, or removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Currently "some post all comments, some regularly screen for profanity and sensitive information," leading to inconsistent availability of abusive or irrelevant material; a uniform approach is recommended to improve integrity and predictability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent flooding and volume-based attacks (spam)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must guard against comments designed to flood the system with irrelevant or bulk submissions that drown out substantive input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of misuse include comments containing entire movie scripts and the text of War and Peace; such volume can overwhelm systems and obscure meaningful comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect against coordinated manipulation by interest groups or foreign actors
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems should be resilient to exploitation that enables interest groups or hostile foreign governments to tilt proceedings in their favor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report highlights "vulnerabilities that interest groups or even hostile foreign governments can exploit to tilt proceedings in their favor," indicating the need for safeguards against coordinated or state-linked manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve meaningful public participation and quality of input
rubrics_metrics.description: Online comment systems should be managed so that public comment periods remain a meaningful avenue for constituents to give input that helps agencies craft better regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release emphasizes that "public comment periods are crucial" and that abuse "drowns out the substantive, significant comments that could make the regulations better," so measures should prioritize ensuring substantive contributions are visible and usable by agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide recourse and protections for identity-theft victims
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should implement procedures to address and remedy instances where stolen identities are used to post comments and to give recourse to victims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report documents "rampant use of stolen identities to post comments on proposed regulations with no recourse for identity theft victims" and calls for better protections and mechanisms for remediation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt recommendations from advisory bodies (ACUS, GAO) and implement identified improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies (and Congress) should consider and implement recommendations from the Administrative Conference of the United States (ACUS), the Government Accountability Office (GAO), and the Subcommittee to improve the online commenting process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Subcommittee held a hearing to review its findings "as well as recommendations from the Administrative Conference of the United States and the Government Accountability Office to improve the online commenting process," indicating these bodies' recommendations form actionable guidance.
